intro.title:
LA Metro Fare Evasion Dashboard
   By Alex Davis        March 2026
intro.blurb: Below is a data-backed estimate of fare evasion on LA Metro, created as part of the Enforce the Fares campaign. Between 2017 and 2020, LA Metro's security department quietly ratcheted down onboard fare checks from around 600,000 a month to just 5,000. Fare evasion skyrocketed, and now, more than half of boardings are unpaid. This policy change cratered fare revenue and worsened safety, but it's not too late to reverse course. To learn more about our campaign to bring back fare checks, visit www.enforcethefares.org.

bus.notes: The fare total for the G Line is calculated by adding together the Station Fare Counts because on the G Line, fares are paid offboard.

This was the bus Metro operated to link the two K Line fragments before the line was completed in June 2025. While its ridership was properly tabulated, its fare data got dumped into the "unclassified" row.

These fares were accidentally attributed to bus routes that were not operating in 2025. They are data errors and represent about 0.14% of the total fares paid. But we are including them anyway because they were likely real fares paid on other routes.
These are also real fares that were paid. We just don't know where because they weren't attributed to any specific route. We believe these are primarily from temporary routes like the 857.

rail.notes: This is likely a result of TAP-to-Exit. In 2025, the TAP-to-Exit pilot caused many B Line fare evaders to end up getting charged at North Hollywood when exiting, resulting in more fares than boardings. To be clear, I freely concede that TAP-to-Exit works at individual stations. My point is that it only works when TSOs are present and that's what's causing the fare compliance, not the tapping proceedure. And we'll never have enough TSOs to babysit even half the system's faregates. TAP-to-Exit is a performative distraction from the real solution: fare checks.

totals.notes: This is the total fare evasion rate for the whole bus system.
This is the fare evasion rate for the stations without in-gate transfers.

When we excluded the in-gate transfer stations, we lowered the total rail ridership in the calculation. So to get the systemwide evasion rate, we have to adjust the rail totals back up to the total for all stations. In other words, we're assuming that on average, the excluded stations had the same evasion rate as the included stations and adjusting the totals as if they were in the calculation. This appropriately weights the relative ridership of Metro's bus and rail systems.
In 2025, 50% of boardings on LA Metro were unpaid.
